programme.desc: Está obsesionada y por celos ataca a la novia de su vecino, él la golpea y ahora ella quiere que la cuide. Yoli quiere el divorcio y la custodia de su hijo porque su esposo come manatíes.

programme.title: Enemigo íntimo
programme.desc: Morillo vigila de cerca, pero lo interceptan y, a menos que colabore, usarán una prueba contra él. Tiene una misión y debe cumplirla rápida y eficientemente, en la misma estación de policía.

programme.title: Enemigo íntimo
programme.desc: Diego tiene pruebas que arruinarían la carrera de Ferrer. Mientras, él debe justificar sus acciones, incluso le recomiendan ayuda profesional en Salud Ocupacional tras golpear a un subalterno.

programme.title: 100 días para enamorarnos
programme.sub-title: Una bomba a punto de explotar
programme.desc: La tensión está en el ambiente. Gloria cuida a Martín y Constanza entra en cortocircuito. Plutarco defiende a su ex y su amante reacciona. Emiliano toca fondo al recibir una mala noticia y Jimena le pide complicidad a Darío.

programme.title: 100 días para enamorarnos
programme.desc: Karla se confiesa con Constanza y le pide que abra su corazón. Sin ánimo de confundir, la abogada confirma que atenderá su caso, pero una cosa no tiene que ver con la otra. Plutarco las ve.

programme.title: Juego de villanos
programme.desc: Dieciocho villanos icónicos compiten por el título de "El Emperador de los Villanos" y 200 mil dólares. Entre desafíos, inmunidades, alianzas y traiciones, solo uno alcanza la cima.

programme.title: Caso cerrado
programme.sub-title: Con todo el peso encima; Iglesia de la marihuana
programme.desc: Cree que su esposa quiere que regrese solo por una herencia, ella pide que se haga un bypass gástrico. La madre exige custodia total de su hija, el papá es pastor de la iglesia de la marihuana.

programme.title: La Doña
programme.desc: Braulio queda a cargo de Miguel Preciado para torturarlo y sacarle información. Mónica se ilusiona con Saúl. Felipe descubre que La Doña lo droga para incapacitarlo sexualmente y tiene un altar secreto.

programme.title: La Doña
programme.desc: Felipe descubre que Altagracia usó su cargo para conseguir los terrenos y se quiere cobrar, en sus carnes, todas las humillaciones. Gabino le roba un beso a Mónica; ella le dice que ama a otro.

programme.title: Victoria
programme.desc: Victoria disfruta una agradable velada en casa de Jerónimo. Él comparte con ella detalles sobre su pasado y ella le habla de sus sueños y deseos, pero una visita inesperada arruina el momento.

programme.title: Victoria
programme.desc: Victoria decide confesarle a su hijo Santiago todo lo que pasa con Jerónimo y él la apoya. Por su parte, Enrique se muda al departamento de Tatiana.

programme.title: Caso cerrado
programme.sub-title: El secreto peligroso; Culpa y capricho
programme.desc: Carolina dice que Patricia oculta un pasado que afecta la relación, ella le reprocha el haberlo destapado. Quiere el divorcio de su esposa porque siente que es un depravado sexual.

programme.title: Caso cerrado
programme.desc: Señalan a Juan de participar en el secuestro y muerte de una parte de la familia de Abel. Debby subasta el agua de unos baños que se dio y su amigo Josué le exige la mitad del dinero ganado.

programme.title: The Price Is Right
programme.desc: "Come on down!" "The Price Is Right" -- hosted by Bob Barker until 2007 and Drew Carey thereafter -- features a wide variety of games and contests with the same basic challenge: Guess the prices of everyday (or not-quite-everyday) retail items. Four contestants, all of whom are seated in one of the wildest audiences in daytime game-show history, are called to the stage to play a preliminary pricing round. That winner joins the host on stage for one of more than 70 different pricing games. After three such games, the contestants spin a big wheel -- hoping to get as close to $1 as possible -- in the "Showcase Showdown." The two highest winners of that round advance to the final, where prizes could be cars or roomsful of furniture. A trio of models presents the prizes.

programme.title: The Price Is Right
programme.desc: "Come on down!" "The Price Is Right" -- hosted by Bob Barker until 2007 and Drew Carey thereafter -- features a wide variety of games and contests with the same basic challenge: Guess the prices of everyday (or not-quite-everyday) retail items. Four contestants, all of whom are seated in one of the wildest audiences in daytime game-show history, are called to the stage to play a preliminary pricing round. That winner joins the host on stage for one of more than 70 different pricing games. After three such games, the contestants spin a big wheel -- hoping to get as close to $1 as possible -- in the "Showcase Showdown." The two highest winners of that round advance to the final, where prizes could be cars or roomsful of furniture. A trio of models presents the prizes.

An FBI agent discovers her ability to read lips and promotes Sue to an elite surveillance team. Suddenly, Sue and her hearing dog, Levi, are "G-Men," involved in a lot more action than they bargained for. This series is loosely based on the real-life deaf FBI agent Sue Thomas.

programme.title: Heartland
programme.desc: This sprawling family saga takes place where an unfortunate tragedy has glued a family together to pull them through life's thick and thin moments. Follow young Amy Fleming as she slowly discovers she possesses her now-deceased mother's ability to aid injured horses as well as maintaining good relationships with those who are trying to get by one day at a time. The family pursues forgotten dreams and challenges as their strength is tested against personal struggles.

programme.title: 60 Minutes
programme.desc: The oldest and most-watched newsmagazine on television gets the real story on America's most prevalent issues. CBS News correspondents contribute segments to each hourlong episode. Topics range from hard news coverage to politics, lifestyle, pop culture, business, health, and science. The correspondents and contributors include Sharyn Alfonsi, Anderson Cooper, Steve Kroft, Lara Logan, Norah O'Donnell, Scott Pelley, Charlie Rose, Lesley Stahl, Jon Wertheim, Oprah Winfrey and Bill Whitaker.

programme.desc: When internationally renowned dancer Pierre Dulaine takes a teaching job in a New York City public school, he meets ridicule from the street-wise students, who scoff at the notion of ballroom dancing. Far from being discouraged, he melds their hip-hop moves with his classical style, helping them create a dance form and, in the process, becoming their mentor.

programme.title: Sweet Dreams
programme.desc: Aspiring country singer Patsy Cline (Jessica Lange) is resigned to both her thankless gigs and her unhappy marriage, until she meets the charismatic Charlie Dick (Ed Harris). Eventually leaving her husband to marry Charlie, Patsy temporarily shelves her performing career to be a mother. Later she returns to singing and finds success under manager Randy Hughes (David Clennon). Patsy hits a remarkable stride with a string of hit singles, and has become a full-fledged star when tragedy strikes.

programme.title: Collision Course
programme.desc: Detroit crime boss Madras hires men to smuggle a top secret, Japanese-made turbocharger into the U.S. But Madras' crooks are murdered, and the turbocharger goes missing. As he searches for the stolen engine, so does straitlaced Tokyo detective Fujitsuka Natsuo. Eventually, local authorities catch wind of the case, and onto the investigation comes brash cop Tony Costas, who must team with his polar opposite, Natsuo, to find the turbocharger.

Each day, "Good Morning Football" brings viewers up-to-the-minute breaking NFL news and local NFL stories on a national platform. The show features a combination of headline-making interviews and a discussion of a wide array of issues in the areas of sports, news and entertainment. By booking celebrity guests and opinionated national and local journalists -- and taking advantage of a close collaboration with all 32 NFL franchises -- "Good Morning Football" breaks out within and well beyond its time period.

programme.title: Live: NFL Total Access
programme.desc: The NFL Network's flagship program airs six nights a week, churning out the day's top headlines and much more covering all 32 teams. The show also provides fans with exclusive footage from inside team facilities and interviews with players and coaches. Joining hosts Dan Hellie and Amber Theoharis with analysis and insight are a deep roster of NFL Network personnel plus other former players as guest analysts throughout each week.

programme.title: NFL Football
programme.desc: The Detroit Lions host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in NFL regular-season play at Ford Field. At 7-2 and winners of five games straight, Detroit welcomes a Tampa Bay side that has dropped six of nine and lost their last game to Chicago, 27-24.

programme.title: NFL Fantasy Live
programme.desc: Millions of NFL fans live in a fantasy world where survival depends on successfully navigating the twists and turns of a grueling season. After all, relying on a second-string quarterback or an untested wide receiver to come up big is usually foolhardy. Avoiding such predicaments takes plenty of preparation, and that's where "NFL Fantasy Live" comes into play. Host Marcas Grant provides the advice and analysis fantasy fans need to make winning lineup decisions. And being armed with the latest player updates, stats and trends goes a long way toward turning fantasies into championships.

programme.title: NFL Live
programme.desc: Host Laura Rutledge takes the helm of this weekday show featuring the likes of Marcus Spears, Dan Orlovsky, Mina Kimes, and Adam Schefter. The "NFL Live" crew entertains fans while offering all the latest news and analysis from across the NFL.

Iola Boylen, Thelma's friend and neighbor, is a frequent visitor to the Harper household, which is often the site of bickering between abrasive Mama and her loved ones. Vicki Lawrence stars as Mama, a character she originated in sketches on "The Carol Burnett Show.".

programme.title: The Price Is Right
programme.desc: "Come on down!" "The Price Is Right" -- hosted by Bob Barker until 2007 and Drew Carey thereafter -- features a wide variety of games and contests with the same basic challenge: Guess the prices of everyday (or not-quite-everyday) retail items. Four contestants, all of whom are seated in one of the wildest audiences in daytime game-show history, are called to the stage to play a preliminary pricing round. That winner joins the host on stage for one of more than 70 different pricing games. After three such games, the contestants spin a big wheel -- hoping to get as close to $1 as possible -- in the "Showcase Showdown." The two highest winners of that round advance to the final, where prizes could be cars or roomsful of furniture. A trio of models presents the prizes.
